meanings.note: 'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: в выходные / на выходных = at the weekend

examples.trans: What are you doing at the weekend?

examples.text: В будни семьсот рублей. В выходные — полторы тысячи.
examples.trans: On weekdays seven hundred roubles. On weekends, fifteen hundred.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Я не поеду на конную прогулку.
examples.trans: I am not going on a horseback ride.
All right, here you go. There, look.
This is equipment for molecular cuisine.
Chef, will you look for a molecular cook?

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.
Can I go and have a look?
It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

examples.text: Я не поеду на конную прогулку.
examples.trans: I am not going on a horseback ride.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.
Just please don't tell my parents.
My parents live in the country.

examples.text: Возьмите свои работы и подарите родителям.
examples.trans: Take your work and give it to your parents.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: At the start of a question.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
